intuition.title: Tetrahedral growth after precursor substitution
intuition.text: Replacing elemental selenium with tributylphosphine selenide produces about 75% fewer initial nuclei. The authors associate fewer nuclei and faster precursor reaction with higher chemical potential per growing particle and tetrahedral growth. The 5.0 nm value is an edge length; triangular ordering on TEM grids describes assembly, not a distinct crystal phase.
intuition.source_locator: Main PDF p. 3, Figure 4 and tetrahedral-growth discussion

intuition.title: Potential scale-up is an outlook
intuition.text: Heating a mixture without rapid precursor injection could simplify process control and scaling, according to the authors. The article does not demonstrate an industrial production run, a scale-up yield, or a validated manufacturing cost.

general_background.title: Heating and precursor conversion
general_background.summary: As a mixture is heated, precursor conversion and particle growth can change at different rates. Different activation barriers can make these rates change differently as temperature rises, allowing nucleation and growth to overlap.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Mechanisms of Nucleation and Growth of Nanoparticles in Solution

general_background.title: From a metal precursor to reactive species
general_background.summary: A metal precursor supplies the metal, while its ligands and conversion chemistry influence how reactive species become available. Stronger or more persistent coordination can slow release of reactive metal species, while ligand exchange can open alternative conversion pathways.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation

reference.title: Mechanisms of Nucleation and Growth of Nanoparticles in Solution

general_background.title: Conversion of a nonmetal precursor
general_background.summary: Chalcogen and pnictogen precursors can differ in how they release or transfer the element during a reaction. Bonding, coordination and the reaction medium can influence the activation or transfer steps that make an element available for growth.
general_background.label: General background, not the authors' interpretation
